segments.t: KorTTY stores all application data and configuration under the KTPH000 directory in your home folder. This guide documents every file and subdirectory, their purpose, and how they are used.
Contains all saved SSH connections with their settings.

KTPH010Includes:KTPH011
- Connection name, host, port, username
- Authentication method (password, SSH key, temporary SSH key)
- Terminal appearance overrides (font, colors, size)
- SSH tunnels and jump server configuration
- Optional per-connection SSH host-key verification override (verify, don't verify, or inherit)
- Optional per-connection character encoding (KTPH000; missing means the default — see KTPH012Terminal → EncodingKTPH013)
- Terminal effect plugins and animation speed
- Connection-specific terminal logging settings
- Per-connection session journal settings (enable, capture typed input, AI summaries, summary interval)
- Window geometry preferences
- Group/folder organization
- Optional free-text tag (used for search, bulk tagging and tag-based export)
- Optional keyword highlighting rule set (KTPH001): the id of a built-in or your own rule set, KTPH002 for no highlighting, or missing to follow the default rule set (see KTPH014Rule set per connectionKTPH015). Connections from a KTPH016teamworkKTPH017 file can carry it as well; the id of a rule set that does not exist on your computer is ignored.
- Optional paste protection that overrides KTPH018Settings → Terminal → Paste protectionKTPH019 for this connection: KTPH003 (KTPH004, KTPH005 or KTPH006) and KTPH007 (0 to 1000; 0 pastes at once). Missing means the global setting, and an unknown warning mode counts as missing (see KTPH020Paste protectionKTPH021). Connections from a KTPH022teamworkKTPH023 file can carry both, but their warning mode applies only when it asks more often than your own setting.
- Optional tab color (KTPH008, KTPH009) that marks the connection's terminal tabs with a colored dot; anything that is not a hex color is ignored (see KTPH024Tab colorKTPH025). Connections from a KTPH026teamworkKTPH027 file can carry it as well, so the file's maintainer decides how those tabs are marked.
KTPH000Security:KTPH001 Connection passwords are encrypted with AES-256-GCM using the master password.

If a connection password is encrypted, it is stored in a hashed/encrypted format and cannot be viewed as plain text. When you open a saved connection, the password is automatically decrypted using your master password.
Centralized credential storage for username/password pairs.

KTPH003Includes:KTPH004
- Credential name, username, password
- Environment (Production, Development, Test, Staging, or one of your own from KTPH000)
- Server pattern (glob patterns like KTPH001 or KTPH002)
- Auto-assignment to connections matching the pattern
KTPH000Security:KTPH001 All passwords are encrypted with AES-256-GCM.
Your own credential environments and the tab colors of all environments (see KTPH000Environments and tab colorsKTPH001).

KTPH002Includes:KTPH003
- Custom environments with their id and display name (KTPH000); the built-in Production, Development, Test and Staging are not stored
- Optional tab colors of built-in and custom environments (KTPH001); a value that is not a hex color, or the color of an environment that no longer exists, is ignored
A file without colors, as earlier versions wrote it, loads unchanged. Without the file korTTY has only the built-in environments, and no environment has a color.

KTPH000Includes:KTPH001
- SSH key path
- Key passphrase (if the key is protected)
- Optional description
- Key fingerprint
KTPH000Security:KTPH001 Key passphrases are encrypted with AES-256-GCM using the master password.

SSH keys referenced in this file can be kept in their original location or copied to KTPH000 via the KTPH001Copy to User DirectoryKTPH002 action in SSH key management. Copied keys are included in encrypted backups; keys left in their original locations are only referenced and must be migrated separately.

The versioned trust-on-first-use store for interactive Terminal and SFTP connections and the SSH bootstrap used by Mosh. Entries are keyed by normalized host name and port and contain the public-key algorithm, OpenSSH SHA-256 fingerprint, OpenSSH public-key line, and trust timestamp. A matching key is accepted silently after first-use confirmation; a changed key is hard-blocked and is not replaced automatically. Entries are replaced through KTPH000Review and Replace…KTPH001 in the changed-key alert and removed under KTPH002Configuration → Security → Known Hosts…KTPH003; removing the last entry deletes the file, which counts as an empty store. When host-key verification is relaxed to accept-new for a connection, an unknown key is pinned without the confirmation prompt — a changed key is still refused in both modes.

Writes use a temporary file plus atomic replacement, while KTPH000 coordinates separate korTTY processes so their pins are merged safely. The properties file is included in encrypted backups; the transient lock file is not. This endpoint-based store is separate from the JobScheduler host-key pins in KTPH001, which are keyed by connection ID for unattended operations.

Remembers which KTPH000SSH tunnelsKTPH001 you allowed korTTY to open: one entry per connection ID with a SHA-256 fingerprint of the server, of whether the connection is your own or shared (Teamwork), and of the enabled tunnels. When a connection's tunnels or its server change, the fingerprint no longer matches and korTTY asks again before it opens them. The file is not part of a backup, so a restored or migrated configuration asks once more; deleting it has the same effect.
Stores GPG key information for backup encryption.

KTPH000Includes:KTPH001
- GPG key ID
- Key email address
- Optional fingerprint
- Import source (system keyring or manual entry)
KTPH000Contains:KTPH001 every preference of the KTPH002Global SettingsKTPH003 dialog, grouped below by the area it belongs to.
UI font size (percent, 80–160%, or auto-derived from the display resolution) and the manual's separate text size (70–250%)
Main-window geometry and state (position, size, maximized status), plus a named geometry entry for every user-resizable application dialog
KTPH000: whether the terminal of a connection with a KTPH001tab colorKTPH002 gets a frame in that color, and a split pane of a connection with a different color a frame of its own (on by default)

KTPH000: the KTPH002tab colors of Connection Manager foldersKTPH003, one KTPH001 entry per folder with a color of its own; an entry whose color is not a hex color is ignored, and without the element no folder has a color
KTPH000: whether a terminal tab shows the KTPH001title its shell setsKTPH002 in place of the connection's name (on by default)
KTPH000: whether KTPH003KTPH001KTPH004+KTPH005KTPH002KTPH006 switches tabs in the order they were last used instead of their KTPH007tab bar orderKTPH008 (off by default)

KTPH000: the absolute paths of the project files you opened or saved last, newest first, at most 10, which KTPH003KTPH004File → Open RecentKTPH005KTPH006 lists; KTPH001: when you last chose KTPH007Clear ListKTPH008 there (milliseconds since 1970, KTPH002 for never)

KTPH000: what korTTY does at startup with the KTPH004previous sessionKTPH005: KTPH001 offers it in a bar (the default, also for a missing or unknown value), KTPH002 restores it once no dialog is open, KTPH003 does nothing

KTPH000: whether a restored session also shows the KTPH002saved output of each terminal paneKTPH003 (off by default); KTPH001: how many lines of output are kept per pane, 100 to 5000 (1000 when missing)
KTPH000: your own KTPH004keyboard shortcutsKTPH005, one KTPH001 entry per changed command, such as KTPH002 or KTPH003; without it every command keeps its default shortcut
Docked live session-journal panel: placement (hidden/left/right) and width
Last ASCII Art dialog preview zoom level
Last ASCII Art picture size (Small to Extra large) for the AI Picture tab, and separately for the Image File tab
Last ASCII Art copy format: comment style, output-code style and gap
Default terminal encoding for SSH connections, and KTPH000, which records that a value stored by an older version has been saved again and applies (see KTPH001Terminal → EncodingKTPH002)

The master switch (KTPH000), highlighting in full-screen programs (KTPH001), the default rule set (KTPH002, the id of a built-in or your own set; empty means none) and whether rules with an action may notify or run their snippet (KTPH003)

Your own rule sets (KTPH000), as edited in the KTPH008rule-set editorKTPH009: each set has a stable id, a name and its rules in priority order, and each rule its id, whether it is on, the pattern, whether it is a regular expression, ignore case, whole word, whether it colors the match or the whole line, the text and background colors (KTPH001, a theme color KTPH002 to KTPH003, or empty to keep the program's color), bold, italic and underline, and its action (KTPH004, KTPH005 or KTPH006), its optional name, whether a notification carries the matched text and the id of the snippet it runs (KTPH007; see KTPH010Notifications for matching outputKTPH011 and KTPH012Running a snippet when output matchesKTPH013). Which connections you allowed a rule's snippet for is not saved: korTTY asks again after a restart
The built-in rule sets are not stored: they come with korTTY, so a new version can improve them, and their ids start with KTPH000, which your own sets cannot use
AI profile defaults, Text/Coding role assignments, embedded GGUF references, prompt presets, and knowledge-store associations
RAG embedding model ID and llama.cpp preferred runtime backend/update policy
AI request timeout in minutes (0 = no limit)
AI summaries (interval and profile) and the AI screenshot analysis toggle
AI line window and token budget
Journal page appearance and live-log tail height
Snippet input-hardening defaults (enabled, options, max file size)
PDF export watermark (off by default; custom text and colour)
Document export footer (on by default; custom text)
SSH host-key verification opt-out: the global flag and the list of connection groups whose checking is relaxed to accept-new
Backup encryption method and retention settings
The atomically written JAXB registry for locally installed or referenced GGUF models.
Stable model ID and display name
GGUF path and compatible KTPH000 executable path
Context size, CPU threads, GPU layers, and idle-unload minutes

The registry contains paths and settings, not model weights or API keys. KTPH000 holds managed GGUF copies, KTPH001 holds independently updated native packages, and KTPH002 holds temporary process directories, logs, and owner-only generated key files. Temporary keys are removed when the sidecar stops.
The regenerable native-runtime area contains immutable package directories plus small atomic state files:
KTPH000 points to the currently selected installation.
KTPH000 records a candidate and its rollback base until a real GGUF-backed authenticated API start succeeds.
KTPH000 retains at most the two newest confirmed, non-revoked installations.
KTPH000 is the durable denylist learned from verified signed indexes; a revoked package also contains KTPH001.
KTPH000 remembers the runtime ID removed from active use by a withdrawal so the UI can explain why local AI remains blocked.
KTPH000 holds the runtime ID the user switched to with KTPH002Other version…KTPH003; while present, update checks keep that version. The MLX runtime area KTPH001 uses a file of the same name.
KTPH000 contains extracted verified installations, while KTPH001 is temporary staging protected by the updater lock.

Do not edit or delete the denylist/quarantine markers to re-enable a package. Runtime launches independently enforce them, and a compatible signed replacement must be installed instead. The entire directory is excluded from backup because packages and state can be recreated from the signed stable channel.

An atomic cache envelope containing the last model/prompt catalog payload and its detached signature. korTTY re-verifies the signature and strict schema before every cache use. If the application has no valid catalog public trust root, this file is ignored and the built-in bootstrap is used without a network refresh. The cache is regenerable and is not included in backups.
The atomically written, owner-readable JSON registry for knowledge stores and their sources.
Store ID/name/type, local snapshot directory or Qdrant endpoint/collection, embedding model ID and vector dimensions

Per-source stable ID, canonical path, file/directory type, enabled flag, automatic/manual sync mode, size limit, include/exclude globs, KTPH000 preference, content hashes, last status, file/chunk/problem counts, and last successful index time

The KTPH000 subdirectory holds regenerable KTPH001 snapshots. A v2 snapshot embeds its format version, vector dimensions, embedding model ID, hierarchical graph parameters, entry point, chunk metadata, vectors, node levels, and per-layer neighbors; a mismatch is rejected and requires a rebuild. A valid legacy single-layer v1 snapshot is rebuilt and atomically migrated when opened.
All JobScheduler jobs and related data.

KTPH000Contains:KTPH001
- Job name, enabled status, action type (COMMAND, SNIPPET_SCRIPT, AI_AGENT, SFTP, RSYNC_SYNC)
- Schedule configuration (weekdays, times, intervals, date ranges)
- Target servers or groups
- Host-key pins (OpenSSH public-key material for unattended execution)
- Sudo passwords for servers and groups (encrypted)
- Journal entries with timestamps, exit codes, and redacted output
- Journal retention settings (auto-delete entries older than 14 days by default)

KTPH000Security:KTPH001
- Host-key pinning is required by default for unattended SSH/SFTP/Rsync execution
- Sudo passwords are encrypted with the master password
- Journal entries are stored with KorTTY-managed secrets redacted before persistence
- Archive passwords and backup encryption credentials are stored encrypted
If the master password is locked and a job needs SSH, sudo, API, or archive secrets, the job is blocked and a journal entry is created explaining the issue.
Saved AI conversations and chat history.

KTPH000Includes:KTPH001
- Chat title and creation timestamp
- Conversation messages and responses
- Associated AI profile used for the chat
- Follow-up prompt history (for context)
KTPH000Note:KTPH001 AI result tabs are not automatically saved. You must explicitly save them from the AI tab using the KTPH002SaveKTPH003 button to add them to this file.

KTPH000Includes:KTPH001
- Snippet name, description, language
- Code content with syntax highlighting metadata
- Category/folder organization
- Tags and metadata
- Target system (Operating System column: Linux, macOS, Windows, etc.)
- Import/export history

KTPH000Features:KTPH001
- Support for JSON/XML/YAML import/export
- Plain-text script export
- ZIP archives with optional password or GPG encryption
- Local syntax highlighting with Monaco editor
- AI-assisted editing and code generation
- Persisted Mermaid diagrams (logical-structure flowchart, sequence, state, class, ER) with stable code-reference node IDs and, for selection-scoped diagrams, the covered line range
- One-liner export with optional script arguments
Stores variable definitions for use within snippets.

KTPH000Includes:KTPH001
- Variable name, value, type
- Scope (local or shared)
- Default values and validation rules
Binary file containing the hashed master password.

KTPH000Security:KTPH001 This file does not contain the actual master password—only a cryptographic hash used to verify the password you enter on startup. If this file is lost or corrupted, you must restart KorTTY and set a new master password (though you will lose access to previously stored encrypted credentials and SSH key passphrases).
If you forget your master password, delete KTPH000 and KTPH001, restart KorTTY, set a new master password, and re-enter your passwords. There is no recovery mechanism for the lost password.

Written only while KTPH000auto-loginKTPH001 is enabled: a copy of the master password, KTPH002obfuscated only — not encryptedKTPH003, with owner-only file permissions. Deleting it (or disabling the option) restores the normal startup prompt.
Text file listing disabled terminal-effect plugin IDs (one per line).
KTPH000Purpose:KTPH001 When you disable a terminal-effect plugin via KTPH002Plugins KTPH004 Terminal EffectsKTPH003, its ID is written to this file so it remains disabled after restart.
Optional user overrides for the coding-agent detection rules, one JSON file per agent (KTPH000, KTPH001, KTPH002).

KTPH000Purpose:KTPH001 A file here replaces the bundled rule file of the same agent entirely. An invalid file is reported in the log as a KTPH002coding-agentsKTPH003 warning and the bundled rules stay in effect. The directory does not exist until you create it. See KTPH004Coding agents → Custom rulesKTPH005.

KTPH000Contains:KTPH001
- Startup messages
- Connection attempts and results
- Terminal session events
- Configuration changes
- Errors and warnings
- Performance metrics (on request via JMX)
KTPH000Rotation:KTPH001 The log file grows throughout the application session. Old logs are not automatically rotated (the log file persists until KorTTY exits or you manually delete it).
Check this file when troubleshooting connection issues, plugin loading problems, or unexpected behavior. Common issues logged here include SSH errors, encryption failures, and import/export problems.
KTPH000Format:KTPH001 GZIP-compressed UTF-8 text, one file per terminal tab of a saved project
KTPH002Naming:KTPH003 KTPH000, referenced by file name from the project's KTPH001 file
KTPH000Purpose:KTPH001 Holds the last visible screen of each terminal tab's primary pane at the time the project was saved — not the scrollback, and not the screens of further split panes.

KTPH001Access:KTPH002 Read only when a project is opened with KTPH003Auto-ReconnectKTPH004 enabled; the text is then shown dimmed, locally, above the new session and is never sent to the server. No history search uses these files. korTTY only reads, writes and deletes plain KTPH000 names directly inside this folder. The files are not encrypted.

Per-connection KTPH001Terminal LoggingKTPH002 does not write here: its generated log files go to the folder configured on the connection's Terminal Logging tab, or to KTPH000 when that folder is left empty.

Default target folder for KTPH000per-connection terminal logsKTPH001 when a connection's log folder field is left empty. File naming, daily rotation, compression and retention follow the connection's logging configuration.

KTPH001Format:KTPH002 KorTTY XML-based project format (KTPH000 files)
KTPH003Naming:KTPH004 User-defined project names with KTPH000 extension (e.g., KTPH001, KTPH002)

KTPH000Contains:KTPH001
- List of open connections/tabs at project save time

KTPH000Purpose:KTPH001 Quickly open a pre-configured set of connections for a specific project or workflow.
KTPH000Usage:KTPH001 Save a project via KTPH002File KTPH006 Save ProjectKTPH003, restore via KTPH004File KTPH007 Open ProjectKTPH005 or the project history menu.

The session snapshots korTTY writes while it runs, so KTPH000File KTPH004 Restore Previous SessionKTPH001 can reopen your windows and tabs after a restart or a crash (see KTPH002Previous sessionKTPH003).
KTPH000 — the open windows and tabs of the running korTTY, rewritten a couple of seconds after each change and once more when korTTY quits, together with the Recently Closed list
KTPH000 — the session before this start, which KTPH002Restore Previous SessionKTPH003 opens; at each start korTTY moves KTPH001 here, but only when that session had at least one tab
KTPH000 — held locked by the korTTY that writes the snapshots; a second korTTY started meanwhile reads them but never writes

KTPH000 — only with KTPH002Settings → Window → Session Restore → Also restore the output of each terminal paneKTPH003 switched on: the newest output of one terminal pane, encrypted with the key of the master password (AES-256-GCM), which the snapshots name by KTPH001; written only while the vault is unlocked and only after the pane showed new output, deleted when the option is turned off, when the master password changes, when a backup is restored and when no saved session names it any more (see KTPH004Restoring the outputKTPH005)

KTPH001Format:KTPH002 XML. The windows and tabs are written like a KTPH003projectKTPH004 with Auto-Reconnect; the Recently Closed list keeps the id of each closed tab's saved connection, its tab group, name and terminal effect. Each snapshot also notes whether korTTY quit normally, whether that run restored its previous session and whether it kept running for a minute afterwards, which tells the next start that korTTY ended right after a restore (see KTPH005At startupKTPH006). While the startup offer waits for an answer, KTPH000 keeps the offered session, so it is offered again if korTTY quits or crashes before you choose.

KTPH002Contains noKTPH003 screen text, scrollback, command timestamps, passwords or temporary SSH keys in the snapshots themselves. The folder each local shell tab and pane was in (an absolute path, used to start the shell there again, see KTPH004Local shells start where you left themKTPH005) and the name of the encrypted file with a pane's output in KTPH000, which project files never carry, may appear here; korTTY accepts a folder only as an absolute path without control characters and a scrollback reference only as a plain name. A file in KTPH001 that does not decrypt with the current master password is deleted.

KTPH003Security:KTPH004 The directory and its files are owner-only (KTPH000 and KTPH001) and are replaced atomically. A snapshot that cannot be parsed is moved aside as KTPH002; one that cannot be read is left in place and not written over until the next start.
KTPH000Backup:KTPH001 Not included in configuration backups: the snapshots describe the windows of this computer.
KTPH003Naming:KTPH004 KTPH000 (e.g., KTPH001 for German, KTPH002 for French)

KTPH000Purpose:KTPH001 Stores translations generated by translation APIs (Google Translate, DeepL, LibreTranslate, Microsoft Translator, or Yandex) when you choose to generate language files via KTPH002Settings KTPH004 TranslationKTPH003.

KTPH000Auto-refresh:KTPH001 When you upgrade KorTTY to a new version, generated language files are marked as outdated. Use KTPH002Settings KTPH004 Translation KTPH005 Regenerate outdatedKTPH003 to refresh them with any new or changed UI keys.

Built-in languages (English, German, Italian, Spanish, Portuguese, French, Croatian, Dutch) are shipped with the application and do not use this directory. This directory is only used for dynamically generated translations.
Optional directory for copied SSH keys.
KTPH000Purpose:KTPH001 Stores copies of SSH keys in one place for backup and migration.

KTPH001How to use:KTPH002
1. Open KTPH003Management KTPH007 Manage SSH Keys...KTPH004
2. Select an SSH key and click KTPH005Copy to User DirectoryKTPH006
3. The key is copied to KTPH000

KTPH000Backup:KTPH001 The key files in this directory are included when you create a backup via KTPH002Edit KTPH006 Create BackupKTPH003 (the archive is AES-256- or GPG-encrypted). On import they are restored with owner-only file permissions, and the import merges: local keys are never deleted, and existing files are only replaced with KTPH004OverwriteKTPH005 enabled.

KTPH000Benefits:KTPH001
- Centralized location for all SSH keys
- Included in encrypted backups
- Easy migration to new machines
Normalized host:port TOFU with OpenSSH SHA-256 fingerprints and fail-closed change detection; the optional per-connection/group/global opt-out relaxes only unknown-key prompting to accept-new
Not encrypted; trusted local code, not sandboxed
All files are stored in the same KTPH000 directory across platforms:
When you create a backup via KTPH000Edit KTPH002 Create BackupKTPH001, the following configuration is included:
All KTPH000 configuration files (connections, credentials, credential environments, SSH key references and passphrases, GPG keys, global settings, JobScheduler, snippets, snippet variables, AI chats)
KTPH000 directory — copied SSH key files (restored with owner-only permissions; imports merge and never delete local keys)
KTPH000 interactive host-key trust store (not its transient KTPH001 file)

Managed GGUF weights, native runtime packages, temporary sidecar data, original source documents, and HNSW snapshots are excluded because they are large or regenerable. The KTPH000 and KTPH001 directories are also not part of a backup, and neither is the auto-login file KTPH002.
The backup is encrypted (password-protected ZIP or GPG) and saved to a location you specify.
Backups are the recommended way to migrate KorTTY to a new machine or to recover from data loss. Create a backup regularly and store it in a safe location.
You can edit KorTTY configuration directly by:
Opening KTPH000 in your file manager or terminal
Editing the XML or JSON file with a text editor
Restarting KorTTY to load the changes

Editing XML/JSON files directly can corrupt your data if not done carefully. Never edit a binary KTPH000 snapshot. Always create a backup before manual editing. For most configuration tasks, use the KorTTY UI instead—it handles encryption, validation, and file format correctly.

KTPH001Configuration file not found:KTPH002
- KorTTY creates the KTPH000 directory and all necessary subdirectories on first launch.
- If a configuration file is missing, KorTTY uses sensible defaults and creates the file on next save.

KTPH001Encryption errors:KTPH002
- If you forget your master password, you must delete KTPH000 and set a new password. Previously encrypted data will be inaccessible.

KTPH001Corrupted XML files:KTPH002
- If a KTPH000 file becomes corrupted, restore from a backup or delete the file. KorTTY will recreate it with defaults on next save.

KTPH002Knowledge-store registry or snapshot cannot be read:KTPH003
- Restore KTPH000 from a backup or recreate the store in the AI Manager. Delete only the affected regenerable KTPH001, then choose KTPH004Update nowKTPH005 to rebuild it from the configured source files.

KTPH000Interactive SSH host key changed:KTPH001
- Do not reconnect until you have verified the new OpenSSH SHA-256 fingerprint with the server administrator and ruled out DNS, routing, or man-in-the-middle problems. KorTTY deliberately blocks the mismatch without retrying or replacing the stored pin.

KTPH003Plugin loading issues:KTPH004
- Check KTPH000 for error messages related to plugin loading (e.g., duplicate IDs, missing services, class loading errors).
- Ensure the plugin JAR is in KTPH001 and contains KTPH002.
- Use KTPH005Plugins KTPH007 Terminal Effects KTPH008 ReloadKTPH006 to refresh the plugin list.

KTPH001Log file size:KTPH002
- KTPH000 grows during the application session. It is not automatically rotated. You can safely delete it while KorTTY is closed.

KTPH002Master password recovery:KTPH003
- There is no recovery for a forgotten master password. If you lose it, delete KTPH000 and KTPH001, restart KorTTY, and set a new password.
